grammarFocus: 间接问句；名词性从句；比较、原因和假设表达综合。
title: The Science Café: A Conversation About Sleep and Learning
instructions: 这是一份模拟的英语听力练习材料，适合B2–C1水平学习者。请先听录音（或阅读录音文本），然后完成10个问题。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（以单选形式呈现）和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。所有解释均为中文，并附有原文证据。本材料为原创模拟内容，并非官方雅思试题。
transcript:
Maya: Hi, everyone. Welcome to the Science Café. I'm Maya, and tonight we're talking about sleep and learning. Our guest is Dr. Sam Lee, a sleep researcher. Sam, thanks for coming.
Sam: Thanks, Maya. It's great to be here.
Maya: So, first question: how does sleep affect learning?
Sam: Well, that's a big question. Basically, sleep helps the brain consolidate memories. What I mean is that during sleep, the brain replays and strengthens what you learned during the day. So if you study before bed, you're more likely to remember it.
Maya: Interesting. Does it matter which stage of sleep you get?
Sam: Yes, it does. Deep sleep, which happens mostly in the first half of the night, is important for facts and figures. REM sleep, which comes later, helps with creative problem-solving and emotional memories.
Maya: So if someone pulls an all-nighter before an exam, that's a bad idea?
Sam: Definitely. You might think you're learning more by staying up, but actually you're reducing your ability to recall. It's better to sleep and review in the morning.
Maya: What about naps? Are they helpful?
Sam: Short naps can be, yes. A 20-minute nap can boost alertness. But if you nap for more than 30 minutes, you might feel groggy. So keep it short.
Maya: And does the time you go to bed matter?
Sam: Consistency is key. Going to bed and waking up at the same time every day, even on weekends, helps your body clock. If you change your schedule a lot, your sleep quality suffers.
Maya: Some people say they can learn during sleep, like listening to recordings while asleep. Is that true?
Sam: That's a common myth. You can't learn new information during sleep. But sleep does help you retain what you learned before. So listening to recordings while asleep won't help you learn a new language, for example.
Maya: OK, so what's one practical tip for our audience?
Sam: Try to review material before bed, and then get a full night's sleep. And avoid screens for an hour before bed, because the blue light can delay sleep.
Maya: Great advice. Thanks, Sam.
Sam: My pleasure.

grammar.title: 间接问句；名词性从句；比较、原因和假设表达综合
grammar.explanation: 本课重点复习间接问句（如'I wonder what...'）、名词性从句（如'What I mean is that...'）、以及比较、原因和假设的表达。间接问句用陈述语序，不用疑问语序；名词性从句在句中充当主语、宾语或表语；比较常用than或as...as；原因常用because或since；假设常用if引导的条件句。
grammar.example: What I mean is that during sleep, the brain replays and strengthens what you learned during the day.

options: Can you tell me where the library is?
Can you tell me where is the library?
Can you tell me where the library?
Can you tell me where is library?
answers: Can you tell me where the library is?
questions.explanation: 间接问句用陈述语序，即'where the library is'，而不是疑问语序'where is the library'。

options: What she said surprised everyone.
What did she say surprised everyone.
What she said did surprise everyone.
What she said surprising everyone.
questions.explanation: 名词性从句'What she said'作主语，谓语用surprised，语序为陈述语序。

options: If I had more time, I would read more.
If I have more time, I would read more.
If I had more time, I will read more.
If I have more time, I will read more.
answers: If I had more time, I would read more.
questions.explanation: 假设条件句表示与现在事实相反，if从句用过去式（had），主句用would + 动词原形。

options: She studies harder than her brother does.
She studies harder than her brother.
She studies more hard than her brother.
She studies harder than her brother is.
answers: She studies harder than her brother does.
questions.explanation: 比较级用harder，than后接比较对象，可用助动词does替代前面的动词。
